workflows.name: Tessellation Paving Workflow
workflows.description: Create custom tessellation patterns for paving areas with full control over geometry and spacing

steps.description: Create a Land Kit area from paving boundary geometry
Apply custom tessellation pattern with manual seam spacing. Seams must be created manually in the tessellation geometry. Origin + U + V points define the copy vectors for pattern generation.
Trim pattern to fit the paving area boundary

steps.component: Add Color Rule or Add Pattern to Area
steps.description: Apply colors or additional styling to tessellation

key_concepts.tessellation_geometry: Closed curve or surface representing one or more base pavers with manual seam spacing
key_concepts.origin_point: Reference location that defines where the pattern starts; U and V points offset from this determine copy vectors
key_concepts.u_point: Horizontal copy vector - defines how pattern copies across X direction
key_concepts.v_point: Vertical copy vector - defines how pattern copies across Y direction
key_concepts.point_of_beginning: Controls where pattern generation originates (defaults to Rhino origin 0,0,0). Important for areas far from origin.
key_concepts.seam_spacing: Manual - must be included in tessellation geometry, not generated automatically
key_concepts.tessellation_preview: 3x3 grid preview showing pattern before full site generation

important_notes: Seam spacing between pavers must be manually created as part of tessellation geometry
Origin, U, and V point spacing controls the final seam width in the generated pattern
Point of Beginning matters for distant geometry - if pattern fails far from Rhino origin, add explicit Point of Beginning
Layer pipeline should be used when pulling geo data (not Geo pipeline)
workflows.use_case: Create fully custom paving patterns that tessellate across any paving area with precise control over geometry and spacing

workflows.name: Areas Collage with Topography Projection
workflows.description: Create landscape areas from layer geometry, collage overlapping areas, project to topography, and bake with layer names

steps.description: Create areas from geometry, preserving layer name and color as persistent metadata. Use layer naming convention: parent::child (e.g., 'areas::concrete' with wildcards like 'areas::*')
Flatten overlapping areas into plan view. Layer names and colors persist through collaging. Output areas maintain all original metadata.

steps.component: Project Paver Meshes (or Project Area Meshes)
steps.description: Project area surfaces/meshes onto topography while keeping them flat. Each projected mesh retains its layer name and color.
Bake hatches with layer names. Use layer name prefix like 'baked area meshes::' to organize. Overwrite mode replaces previous bakes (e.g., 'areas projected' replaces every bake).

key_concepts.layer_naming: Use parent::child convention (areas::concrete, areas::green, areas::*). Wildcard '*' matches any child layer.
key_concepts.data_persistence: Layer names, colors, and geometry metadata stay associated through collaging, clipping, and projection operations
key_concepts.collaging: Flattens overlapping areas into a clean plan. Each resulting area retains its source layer name and color.
key_concepts.projection: Keeps areas flat but repositions them to follow topography. Useful for visualization and baking.
key_concepts.baking: Converts digital areas to Rhino geometry with layer organization. Overwrite mode updates existing bakes.
key_concepts.overwrite_baking: Anything named 'areas projected' (or specified bake name) gets replaced on each bake. Prevents duplication.

important_notes: Layer names and colors persist through all operations (collaging, clipping, projection, baking)
Use double-colon (::) to define parent::child layer relationships; wildcard (*) matches any child layer
Surfaces and closed curves work; B-reps (Rhino 8) work but may need updates for Rhino 7
Bake name should include prefix (e.g., 'baked area meshes::' or 'areas projected') to organize output layers
Overwrite mode replaces old baked geometry - useful for iterative design workflows
workflows.use_case: Design complex landscape areas with layer organization, collage overlapping zones, project to site topography, and generate organized CAD geometry for visualization or construction docs

workflows.name: Curb Cuts and Live Topography Editing
workflows.description: Edit topography in real-time by cutting and modifying curbs, with live preview and parametric control

steps.description: Create topography from existing surface or mesh. Define break lines to guide modification logic.

Cut and modify curbs with parametric control. Curb curves are plan view (elevation doesn't matter for curve position). Curb spots define elevation. Tolerances control how close curves/points must be to match.
Patch curb cuts into existing topography. Not necessary if not patching. Breaklines and boundaries keep topography logical.
Visualize and bake topography. Live editing - no refresh needed. Bake name replaces previous geometry on each bake.

key_concepts.live_editing: Real-time topo updates without refresh. Change parameters and see immediate results.
key_concepts.curb_curves: Plan view geometry - elevation position doesn't matter for curve matching
key_concepts.curb_spots: Points that define curb elevation. Position matters - must be close enough to curves to associate (controlled by curb_spot_tolerance)

curb_cut_parameters.center_line: Line defining where curb cut is located
curb_cut_parameters.width: Width of the curb cut opening

tolerances.curb_tolerance: How close curves need to be together to be matched into one curb
tolerances.curb_spot_tolerance: How close points must be to curves to be associated as elevation control

key_concepts.break_lines: Define how topography changes logically. Keep patch boundaries clean and intentional.
key_concepts.patch_boundary: Curve that defines where patch topo meets existing topo. Creates logical edge.

important_notes: Curb curves are 2D (plan) - elevation doesn't matter for curve position, only for matching
Curb spots (points) define actual curb elevation - must be positioned correctly and close enough to curves
Set curb_spot_tolerance carefully - too loose and points associate with wrong curves
Break lines keep topology intentional - can move patch boundary to adjust logic
Live editing means changes apply instantly - useful for iterative design
Bake name with bake button replaces previous geometry - good for non-destructive iteration
Curb cuts can be used creatively (e.g., wall entrances) beyond traditional curb applications
parametric_flexibility: Adjust width, run, flare while watching live preview
Move curb spots to change elevation while cuts update
Adjust tolerances if curves/points aren't matching correctly
Change patch boundary to adjust how topo patches into existing surface
workflows.use_case: Edit topography parametrically with live feedback, creating curb cuts and ramps that patch into existing terrain while maintaining logical topology

workflows.name: Advanced Topography with Features (Paths, Stairs, Walls, Curbs)
workflows.description: Create complex topography with integrated landscape features - paths, stairs, walls, and curbs pulled from Rhino layers with live editing

steps.description: Pull geometry from Rhino layers. Automatically updates when layer contents change. Define layer path and specify what types to import.
Generate paths by finding nearest point to centerline. Parameters: path width and path slope. Can publish parameters to remote panel for live editing.
Create stairs from surface with defined rise. Publish rise to remote panel for live adjustment.

Create walls from front/back curves with elevation from points. Tolerances control curve pairing (curve_tolerance) and point association (spot_tolerance). spot_tolerance < curve_tolerance < wall width.
Similar to Create Walls - front/back curves with elevation points. Same tolerance logic applies.
Preview and bake individual features. Bake name replaces previous geometry with same name on each bake.
Combine all feature types into one dataset for topography generation.
Pull topo framework from GeoSet layer in Rhino.
Generate topography integrating all features. Division parameters control contour/break line subdivision. Angle tolerance controls smoothness.
Visualize and bake final topography to 'topo mesh' layer and contours to 'topo contours' layer.

key_concepts.layer_pipeline: Auto-updates from Rhino layers when geometry changes. Layer Pipeline (replaces Geometry Pipeline) pulls directly from layer path specification.

tolerances.curve_tolerance: How close curves must be to pair together (for walls/curbs)
tolerances.spot_tolerance: How close points must be to associate with curves (for elevation). Must be < curve_tolerance and < wall width

key_concepts.feature_types: Paths (with slope), Stairs (with rise), Walls (from paired curves), Curbs (similar to walls)
key_concepts.live_editing: Publish parameters to remote panel to adjust width, slope, rise, tolerances without leaving Rhino
key_concepts.merge_features: All features combine into single dataset before topography generation
key_concepts.topo_geoset: Separate layer containing contours, elevation spots, and break lines that define topo framework
key_concepts.bake_workflow: Each feature and final topo baked to named layers. Bake name replaces previous geometry for iterative design

important_notes: Geometry pipeline pulls directly from Rhino - changes to layer update automatically
Curve tolerance and spot tolerance are critical for correct feature generation
spot_tolerance must be smaller than curve_tolerance to avoid point-curve association errors
All parameters can be published to remote panel for live editing without Grasshopper window
Features must be merged before creating final topography
Topo GeoSet is separate from feature layers - contains contours and break lines
Multiple features can be baked independently for preview before final topo generation
Bake name convention: layer names match bake names for automatic overwrite on iteration
workflow_hints: Publish path_width, path_slope, rise, and tolerances to remote panel first
Test individual features (draw/bake paths, stairs, walls separately) before merging
Adjust tolerances carefully - too loose causes incorrect pairing, too tight prevents pairing
Keep Rhino layers panel and Grasshopper remote panel visible simultaneously for efficiency
Use meaningful layer and bake names for quick iteration
workflows.use_case: Create sophisticated topography with integrated features (paths, stairs, walls, curbs) with live parameter control and automatic layer synchronization from Rhino

workflows.name: Constrained Plant Design
workflows.description: Design planting schemes by querying plant database, creating plant instances, and placing them with niche constraints and environmental analysis

steps.description: Define the planting area boundary. Can be a closed curve or trimmed surface.
Create a filter/query for plant database lookup. Define search criteria using field names and values. Use includes/excludes to refine selection.
Query plant database and retrieve species matching all criteria. Returns list of available plants for design.

inputs: species (string, optional - auto-generated if not specified)
steps.description: Define individual plant with species, height, spacing, and optional niche constraints. Can create single or multiple plant types.
If using environmental constraints (sun, soil moisture, etc.), create environment with relevant analysis layers.

Place plants in area while respecting niche constraints and environmental rules. Environment layers provide constraint data (sun, moisture, soil, etc.). Returns placed + unplaced plants for design iteration.

steps.component: Get Plant Info or Get Area Plants
steps.description: Extract plant information from placed plants. Can filter by species, size, or other attributes.

steps.component: Bake Plant Blocks or Draw/Export Plants
steps.description: Visualize planted design in Rhino and generate plant schedule for documentation.

key_concepts.plant_query: Database filter using field-value pairs. Examples: 'Soil Moisture=Moist', 'Sun Requirement=Full Sun', 'Distribution USA=PA'
key_concepts.plant_instance: Individual plant with species, height, radius, color, and optional niche constraints
key_concepts.niche: Defines plant compatibility rules and constraints (e.g., sun exposure range, soil type, moisture requirements)
key_concepts.environment_constraints: Optional environment layers (hours_of_sun, elevation, etc.) that constrain plant placement
key_concepts.add_plants_constrained: Solver that places plants while respecting niche rules and environment constraints. Returns placed + unplaced for iteration.
key_concepts.plant_spacing: self_spacing defines spacing from this plant to itself; cluster_radius groups similar plants
key_concepts.fixed_plants: Can lock certain plants in place during packing/optimization

important_notes: Plant species can be auto-generated or specified by name
Environment is optional but enables constraint-based placement (sun, moisture, soil type, etc.)
Add Plants Constrained returns both placed and unplaced plants - iterate if needed
Plant query can use multiple field-value pairs to narrow selection
Niche constraints prevent placement outside acceptable ranges
Can create multiple plant types and add them together to same area
Plant fill operations automatically prevent plants from being placed outside the planting area boundary - point culling is not necessary
workflow_options: Simple: Define area → Create plants → Add plants (no constraints)
Database-driven: Query database → Get plants → Create instances → Add constrained
Environmentally-constrained: Create environment → Define niches → Query plants → Place with constraints
Multi-species: Create multiple plant types → Combine in single Add Plants step
workflows.use_case: Design ecologically-appropriate planting schemes by querying plant databases, creating plant instances, and placing them with environmental and niche constraints

workflows.name: AI Plugin User Experience Best Practices
workflows.description: Design patterns and best practices for AI-generated Grasshopper plugins to improve usability, reliability, and user control
workflows.context: These patterns guide AI tools in creating intuitive, maintainable, and user-friendly plugin definitions. They prioritize user agency, clear workflow control, and professional output organization.

patterns.description: Expose important parameters, inputs, and outputs to Grasshopper Panel (or RCP Panel) for user accessibility. Open Grasshopper Panel automatically if MCP allows.
guidelines: Publish key parameters (dimensions, thresholds, counts) that users may want to adjust iteratively
Include toggles and sliders for boolean/numeric controls
Publish layer inputs so users can swap source geometry without editing definitions
Label bake buttons clearly and specifically: 'BAKE Topo', 'BAKE Hatches', 'BAKE Paver Meshes', etc. (not generic 'Bake' buttons)
Organize published parameters logically - group related controls
Consider opening Grasshopper Panel automatically if the MCP/plugin system supports it for immediate visibility
patterns.benefit: Users retain control without editing the definition. Labeled buttons make workflows obvious and prevent accidental outputs.

patterns.description: Use Layer Pipeline components (not Geometry Pipeline) for automatic geometry updates from Rhino layers.
guidelines: Replace Geometry Pipeline with Layer Pipeline for all layer-based geometry pulls
Layer Pipeline automatically updates when layer contents change in Rhino
Define clear layer path specifications (e.g., 'DESIGN::PATHS', 'DESIGN::WALLS')
Avoid manual geometry selection - automation reduces friction
patterns.benefit: Workflows stay synchronized with Rhino layers. Users can edit geometry directly in Rhino without rebuilding definitions.

patterns.description: When ingesting multiple related sublayers (e.g., AREAS::CONCRETE, AREAS::LAWN, AREAS::BIODYNAMICFARM, AREAS::BIOSWALE), use wildcard patterns to pull all matching layers.
guidelines: Use 'AREAS::*' to capture all child layers under AREAS (e.g., AREAS::CONCRETE, AREAS::LAWN, AREAS::BIOSWALE)
Avoid hardcoding individual sublayer names - wildcards scale with new layers added by users
Layer names should follow parent::child convention for wildcard matching to work
Communicate naming convention to users if not already established
patterns.example: Layer Pipeline with layer path 'AREAS::*' automatically pulls AREAS::CONCRETE, AREAS::LAWN, AREAS::BIOSWALE and any other child layers
patterns.benefit: Scalable and flexible - users can add new sublayers without breaking definitions.

patterns.pattern: Area Output Layer Naming for Baking
patterns.description: Modify area layer names before baking to prevent writing to layers connected to Layer Pipeline components/listeners.
guidelines: If ingesting from 'AREAS::*', replace 'AREAS' prefix with 'MATERIALS' in output layer names
Examples: 'AREAS::CONCRETE' → 'MATERIALS::CONCRETE', 'AREAS::LAWN' → 'MATERIALS::LAWN'
This prevents feedback loops where baked geometry is re-consumed by Layer Pipeline listeners
If outputting multiple geometry types (e.g., Area Linework AND Draw Areas as Meshes), route each to separate, distinct layers
Never bake two outputs to the same layer - organize by feature type or feature name
patterns.benefit: Prevents data corruption and feedback loops. Keeps input and output layers logically separated.

patterns.description: Use Customize Parameters when collecting unique parameters for individual geometry pieces. Use judiciously - only when necessary.
guidelines: Implement Customize Parameters only if the workflow clearly requires per-geometry customization (e.g., different colors, materials, or settings per area)
Use Sort Key Values to manage key-value output from Layer Pipeline in these workflows
Pair Customize Parameters with Layer Pipeline for robust geometry-to-parameter mapping
Avoid over-implementing - if a single parameter set works for all geometry, use it globally
Document the customization requirement so users understand when to use Customize Parameters
patterns.benefit: Preserves per-object metadata without cluttering simpler workflows. Keeps definitions maintainable.

patterns.pattern: Preview and Bake with Bake+Preview Components
patterns.description: Use Bake+Preview components in Land Kit to show final results and important process steps with live feedback.
guidelines: Use Bake+Preview for outputs that users need to see iteratively (areas, meshes, linework)
Provide unique, meaningful bake names or concatenate prefixes with layer names (e.g., 'baked_topo', 'areas::preview', 'materials::hatches')
Keep preview toggles ON for key outputs so users see results without baking
Use preview for intermediate steps if the plugin generates multi-stage results
Include descriptive labels on toggle buttons: 'Preview Topography', 'Preview Areas', etc.
patterns.benefit: Immediate visual feedback. Users see results in real-time without manual baking, reducing iteration time.

patterns.pattern: Text Output and Labeling with Bake Text
patterns.description: Use Bake Text for text-based outputs (contour labels, spot elevations, plant schedules, bloom calendars, etc.) where text visualization matters.
guidelines: Bake Text does not currently preview, so consider two approaches:
A) Include a text 3D preview component separately for cases where text placement requires user verification before baking
B) Use a bake name with the bake toggle ON - geometry updates automatically on each run, allowing iterative refinement
Simpler approach preferred: set bake toggle to true, keep bake name consistent so it re-bakes and updates each iteration
For complex text layouts (multi-line schedules, labels), provide preview feedback so users can approve placement
Label bake text buttons clearly: 'BAKE Contour Labels', 'BAKE Plant Schedule', 'BAKE Bloom Calendar'
patterns.benefit: Text output is visible and controllable. Users can refine text placement and content through multiple iterations.

patterns.pattern: Plant Output with Bake Plant Blocks
patterns.description: When outputting plants, use Bake Plant Blocks with a boolean toggle set to true and overwrite enabled.
guidelines: Route all plant output through Bake Plant Blocks component
Add a boolean toggle (set default to true) to control baking on/off
Enable overwrite mode to replace previous plant blocks on each bake (prevents duplication)
Label toggle clearly: 'Bake Plants' or 'Plant Output'
Use consistent bake name for all plant outputs so they update together
patterns.benefit: Clean plant block management. Prevents duplicate blocks and ensures plant data always reflects current design.

patterns.pattern: Hatch Plans with Bake Areas as Hatches
patterns.description: Use Bake Areas as Hatches component for hatch-based output (material plans, planting plans, etc.).
guidelines: Route area data through Bake Areas as Hatches for pattern-filled output
Use layer naming convention to organize hatches (e.g., 'hatches::concrete', 'hatches::lawn')
Enable overwrite mode for iterative design
Pair with Clear Previous Bakes if replacing older hatch sets
Label clearly: 'BAKE Hatches' or 'BAKE Materials Plan'
patterns.benefit: Professional hatch output ready for documentation. Clean layer organization for CAD export.

patterns.description: Un-preview all non-essential geometry components, particularly duplicate geometry or intermediate processing steps.
guidelines: Keep preview ON only for key outputs (final areas, final topography, final plants, final linework)
Turn preview OFF for duplicate geometry or intermediate processing (intersection calculations, temporary arrays, etc.)
Hide preview for components that show intermediate states of data transformation
This keeps the 3D view clean and focused on the final design
Use preview strategically - more previews = visual clutter = slower iteration
patterns.benefit: Uncluttered 3D preview. Users focus on design results, not intermediate calculations. Better performance.

patterns.description: Label components for clarity. Use one of two approaches: grouping with component names (Bifocals style) or single panel with numbered list.
guidelines: Approach A (Bifocals style): Group related components and use the group name to label the component (e.g., group named 'Layer Pipeline' containing Layer Pipeline component)

Approach B (Number labels): If plugin uses number labels (like Raven does), create a single panel with returns between items:
  1 - Layer Pipeline
  2 - Create Area
  3 - Sort Key Values
  4 - Add Plants Constrained
  5 - Bake Plant Blocks
Choose one approach consistently - don't mix both
Number labels work well for complex definitions with many steps - easy to reference in documentation
Component groups work well for simpler, more visual definitions
patterns.benefit: Clear workflow navigation. Users understand component order and purpose without reading definitions.

workflows.workflow_summary: These patterns define a user-centric approach to AI plugin design: publish controls explicitly, automate geometry synchronization with Layer Pipeline, separate inputs from outputs, use clear baking conventions, preview selectively, and label everything consistently. The result is a professional, maintainable plugin that respects user agency and scales with design changes.

anti_patterns.problem: Users must edit the definition to adjust controls - friction and risk of breaking connections
anti_patterns.fix: Publish all adjustable parameters to Grasshopper Panel with clear labels

anti_patterns.anti_pattern: Using Geometry Pipeline instead of Layer Pipeline
anti_patterns.problem: Manual geometry selection breaks when users modify Rhino layers
anti_patterns.fix: Replace with Layer Pipeline and layer path specifications

anti_patterns.anti_pattern: Baking to the same layer as Layer Pipeline input
anti_patterns.problem: Creates feedback loop - baked geometry is re-consumed by Layer Pipeline, corrupting data
anti_patterns.fix: Rename output layers (e.g., AREAS → MATERIALS) to separate inputs from outputs

anti_patterns.anti_pattern: Leaving preview ON for all geometry
anti_patterns.problem: 3D view becomes cluttered, performance degrades, user can't focus on results
anti_patterns.fix: Preview only key outputs; hide intermediate calculations and duplicate geometry

anti_patterns.problem: Users don't know what each button does - risk of wrong outputs baking
anti_patterns.fix: Label buttons specifically: 'BAKE Topo', 'BAKE Hatches', 'BAKE Paver Meshes', etc.

anti_patterns.problem: Adds complexity and overhead - slows down simple workflows
anti_patterns.fix: Use Customize Parameters only when per-geometry customization is clearly necessary

workflows.use_case: Guide AI assistants in generating professional, user-friendly Grasshopper plugins that prioritize clarity, automation, and user control

Calculate CN Layer: layer-producing components (Add Shape Values Layer, etc)
Add Tessellation Pattern: area-producing components (Create Land Kit Area, etc)

common_patterns.approach: Use 'Add Shape Values Layer' with curves/areas from Rhino that represent zones
common_patterns.example: Import soil survey boundaries -> Add Shape Values Layer with HSG codes

common_patterns.approach: Stack multiple 'Add Shape Values Layer' calls, each adding a different data type
common_patterns.note: Order doesn't matter for non-overlapping data; overlapping areas use last-added value

common_patterns.approach: Use 'Add Layer by Formula' to create new layers from existing ones
Use component outputs or 'Draw' components to visualize; optional CSV export on some components
common_patterns.example: Calculate CN Layer can export detailed CSV with areas, CN values per catchment
